newsitem.title: USA: Penn buys Pocono Downs for $47 million.
newsitem.headline: Penn buys Pocono Downs for $47 million.

text.p: Penn National Gaming Inc. said Monday it entered a definitive agreement to buy Pocono Downs Inc., owner of the Pocono Downs horse racing facility and two off-track wagering facilities, for $47 million.
Penn said the acquisition, expected to close by Nov. 30, will give it "strong year-over-year earnings gains throughout fiscal 1997 and into 1998."
Pocono Downs is a 400-acre harness racing track in Wilkes Barre, Pa. The company also operates one off-track wagering facility in Allentown and one in Erie.

Penn owns and operates Penn National Race Course, one of two thoroughbred racetracks in Pennsylvania, as well as five off-track wagering facilities in Reading, Chambersburg, York and Lancaster in Pennsylvania.
Wyomissing, Pa.-based Penn said it will finance its Pocono Downs purchase with cash and public and/or bank debt.

Penn also said it now expects third-quarter earnings per share to approximate those of the 1995 third quarter, when it had supplemental pro forma net income of $1.4 million, or 32 cents a share, on revenues of $15.4 million.
The earnings per share is equivalent to 21 cents a share after a three-by-two stock split in May.
Prior estimates for 1996 third quarter ranged from 29 cents to 27 cents per share, said Penn Chief Financial Officer Robert Ippolito.

Penn said the adjusted estimates arise from delays in the opening of its Lancaster off-track wagering facility due to opposition from local groups and the approval of its liquor license, as well as lower-than-expected revenues.
In addition, Penn said its revenues also suffered as it offered free admission and free alcoholic and soft beverages during the Lancaster facility's first 30 days.
In 1995 Pocono Downs and its two off-track wagering facilities generated $173.5 million in gross wagering, an 11 percent increase over 1994, Penn said.
Penn plans to build three more Pocono Downs off-track wagering units over the next 18 months because Pocono Downs is authorised to operate five such facilities.
Penn's stock rose $4.25 to $28.75 on Nasdaq at mid-morning.
